column1: # Product-name occurrences inside ported string literals, one per line
# (docs/status.md 3.73).  PORTING.md 0.1-19 forbids the product name in a
# comment, a version line or a copied declaration block (`tools/check-declarations.py`
# fails on those outright); a *literal* is ported semantics - C's own string -
# and the docstring gate compares it with the reference, so it is counted here,
# with the reason the literal cannot be changed.  Columns:
# <path>\t<class>\t<count>\t<line>\t<reason>.  A count that no longer matches,
# a row nothing matches, and a finding with no row are all failures.
# The rule's ninth half (status 3.613, 2026-10-05) emptied the identity half of this table:
# the reference's bug address and the carried Haiku bundle signature are *this program's*
# outward identity, so they are this repository's own now (the four `.cc` lines are recorded in
# `carried-substitutions.tsv`), and the `DEFVAR_LISP` docstring that named the reference's
# mailing list says this repository's name.  What is left is the one class that is not a
# self-declaration: the licensor's name and the licence text (COPYRIGHT, the GPL banner
# sentence), which a port cannot rename without writing a false attribution.
# The rule's thirteenth half (status 3.648): the *fragment* forms are in the gate's table now, so
# this class is enumerated instead of invisible.  Every row of it is an external name - a registry
# path, a Start Menu folder or shortcut name, an MCI device alias, a window class - which the
# program does not own and cannot rename without changing behaviour.
